solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nan told wimp off for hoax with skull

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, telling us these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A grandmother scolds a weakling, apparently in connection with a fake skull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal on NAN TOLD WIMP. Piltdown Man was a famous fraud: skull fragments 'found' in Sussex in 1912 and exposed as a fake in 1953.
explanation.definitionFit: The Piltdown fossil was a forged early human cranium, one of science's best-known frauds.

clue.text: Suggest one wears mail

indicators.note: the mail wears the one, so the numeral sits inside the word for letters

parts.note: mail means post, the letters delivered
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A proposal that somebody should put on chain mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mail' looks like armour, but it is the postal kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea as a basis for argument, so to propose it.

clue.text: Looking miserable, having been confronted for ages

parts.note: for ages means for a long time, long
been confronted means faced

explanation.surface: Someone looks glum after a lengthy confrontation.
explanation.definitionFit: A long face is the drawn, gloomy expression of somebody unhappy.

clue.text: One introducing music reading out two letters

indicators.note: reading out the letters means saying their names, which spells the entry by its spoken form

parts.note: the two letters are D and J, the abbreviation for disc jockey

explanation.surface: A radio presenter introduces records and spells something aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters D and J are named in speech as 'dee' and 'jay', and that spoken form is the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey presents and plays recorded tracks, introducing each one to listeners.

clue.text: We had married

explanation.surface: A couple say they were once husband and wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We had' contracts to we'd; drop the apostrophe for the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wed is the past participle of the verb for joining in matrimony.

clue.text: Am actor changing musical direction

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer announces he is switching to a new instruction in the score.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcato is an Italian instruction in a score telling players to accent each note.

clue.text: Prime minister protects Tyneside town

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister from 1770 to 1782
protects means shields

explanation.surface: The head of government is said to guard a town in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around the River Tyne in north-east England; North Shields stands on the river's north bank.
explanation.definitionFit: North Shields is a port town on the northern bank of the Tyne estuary.

clue.text: March of Helen? Wrong — of Welshmen

definitions.text: March of Helen? Wrong — of Welshmen

indicators.note: wrong tells us the words before it are put into a mistaken order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a title: the march is not Helen's but belongs to the Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' is the anagram signal on MARCH OF HELEN, and the whole clue then describes the result: a march that belongs to Welshmen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous Welsh military song, the regimental march of Welsh soldiers.

clue.text: Vital part of German city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A German city's church is described as its most important feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital part of' looks like it picks letters, but 'Vital part' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its core, the indispensable quality at its heart.

clue.text: Endure repulsive piece he painted

indicators.note: piece means a portion of the words before it, here a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone must put up with a nasty bit of work he painted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap between ENDURE and REPULSIVE. Albrecht Dürer was the German Renaissance artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The German Renaissance master was a painter and printmaker, so his name fits 'he painted'.

clue.text: Without a second thought, had fun too excitedly

indicators.note: excitedly suggests the letters are thrown about in agitation, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed themselves too wildly without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing something out of hand means rejecting it at once, without consideration.

clue.text: Block a view of Syrian city

parts.note: to block a flow is to dam it
a view is a scene

explanation.surface: A building obstructs the vista over Syria's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'of Syrian city' stands for belonging to Damascus.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene describes things from Damascus, Syria's capital.

clue.text: Tree, or its remains?

definitions.meaning: a common deciduous tree with winged seeds
what is left when the tree, or any wood, is burnt: the powdery residue of a fire

explanation.surface: A question about a tree and what is left of it.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the tree and the grey residue left after burning.

clue.text: Seize greeting card

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
the jack is a playing card, the knave

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a greetings card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greeting card' reads as one item, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to take control of a vehicle or plane by force, so to seize it.

clue.text: Sounded like Christmas bells?

parts.note: the carol 'Jingle Bells' points to the light ringing of small bells, as on a sleigh

explanation.surface: A question about the noise festive bells made.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bells make a light ringing tinkle, the sound named in the famous carol title.

clue.text: Call for quiet, keeping debate calm

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the call for quiet surrounds the other piece

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
to moot is to raise for debate; a moot is a debating assembly

explanation.surface: Someone asks for silence so that a discussion stays peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth water or a smooth manner is calm, free of disturbance.

clue.text: Admitted a vendor initially unpaid

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: money still unpaid is owed

explanation.surface: A seller confessed to an outstanding debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Avowed means openly declared or acknowledged, so confessed.

clue.text: Ladder, or short part of one

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a rung is a step, part of a ladder, the 'one' of the clue

explanation.surface: A ladder, or a small part of a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladder' is the British word for a run in tights or stockings; 'one' refers back to a ladder for climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a ladder in a stocking is a line of unravelled stitches, a run.

clue.text: Girl is in sight, with potential to be cut up

definitions.text: with potential to be cut up

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
something in sight is visible

explanation.surface: A girl comes into view, and she might get upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' suggests being upset, but here it means split into parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be split into parts, as a number by another without remainder, is divisible.

clue.text: Holiday snap

definitions.meaning: to snap is to fracture or crack in two

explanation.surface: A holiday photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a short vacation and to fracture something suddenly.

clue.text: Great success, putting chapter into back story

indicators.note: putting the chapter somewhere places it as a piece in the other word
into says the chapter goes inside the reversed word for story
back means the word for story is read backwards

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A writer triumphs by adding a chapter to a back story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back story' reads as a character's history, but 'back' reverses TALE to give ELAT, and 'putting into' places C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant success or striking effect, as in a triumph carried off with dash.

clue.text: Drink is golfer's support, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a tee is the peg that holds a golf ball before driving

explanation.surface: A golfer claims his drink keeps him going.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is the hot beverage brewed from dried leaves.

clue.text: Little Kenneth died, Saturday or Sunday

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
Ken is short for Kenneth

explanation.surface: A short man called Kenneth passed away on Saturday or Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Either of the two days at the end of the working week is part of it, a definition by example.

clue.text: Child looking for this game

parts.note: a child searching for others who are concealed is playing a well-known game

explanation.surface: A child is searching for a game to play.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's game one player searches for others who have concealed themselves.
